_Majd Asadi at a protest in Umm al-Fahm, 2025._

Earlier this month (March 2), Israeli police [arrested and
jailed](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-politics/2026-03-04/ty-
article/.premium/israeli-arab-activist-arrested-for-facebook-post-on-
khameneis-killing/0000019c-b988-df64-a59c-fbfec0770000) Majd Asadi, a
Palestinian citizen of Israel, on charges of “incitement” and support for
“terrorism.” Asadi is an opera
[singer](https://www.instagram.com/p/DDp2zQstPQ4/?hl=en) and activist from
Daliyat al-Karmel, a town in northern ’48 Palestine. He had written a Facebook
post critical of the US-Israeli war on Iran. It appeared after Israel,
[aided](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/3/inside-the-us-israel-plan-to-
assassinate-irans-khamenei) by the CIA,
[assassinated](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/4/iranians-to-bid-
farewell-to-khamenei-as-israel-threatens-to-kill-successor) Ayatollah Ali
Khamanei, also killing his daughter and grandchild.

In his post, Asadi had dared to say that it was a good thing that under
Khamanei, Iran hadn’t surrendered to Western imperialists. He also added that
the US-Israeli war was motivated by wanting to control Iran’s oil and
resources. The authorities considered this a form of “identification” with a
“terrorist” organization (the Iranian government).

Asadi’s words rained on the parade of [most
Israelis](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2026-03-05/ty-
article/.premium/most-israelis-back-iran-war-but-support-low-among-arab-
citizens-poll-shows/0000019c-be5a-d7b3-affe-befbd9150000), who
[cheer](https://x.com/ireallyhateyou/status/2028376774103474663?s=20) for the
bombing of Iran almost as aggressively as they cheer for the bombing of Gaza.
In an interview last Friday, Asadi explained that he deliberately wrote in
Hebrew in addition to Arabic, so that Israelis get a dose of truth that
Zionist media would never air. He views the use of the Hebrew language as a
political weapon. “I want to disrupt the supremacist use [by Zionists] of
Hebrew, without in any way coddling Israeli readers,” he said. And since Asadi
is a vocal supporter of BDS and outspoken [against the genocide in
Gaza](https://www.middleeasteye.net/opinion/gaza-genocide-there-nothing-
occupy-city-itself-no-longer-exists), Israeli authorities were happy for any
pretext to punish him.

For his post, Asadi was arrested and jailed in the notorious [Megiddo
prison](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/palestinian-teenager-dies-
notorious-israeli-megiddo-prison). Prison authorities shaved Asadi’s head,
just as the German Nazis did in their concentration camps. This practice is
[reserved](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/israel-prison-palestinian-star-
david-shaved-head) for Palestinians; Jewish dissidents don’t have their heads
shaved in the Israeli prison system. Asadi was also threatened with
[torture](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4iGzi3m9QTg), which Palestinian
prisoners – especially those without citizenship – are regularly subjected to.
Megiddo prison is known to use [sexual
violence](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T2eNb-0Fsbw), [tear
gas](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn7vje365rno), dogs, and [infectious
disease](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/advocacy-group-warns-health-
disaster-among-palestinian-detainees-israeli-prison) against prisoners. Last
year, a 17-year-old Palestinian from Silwad (in the West Bank) was
[martyred](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/palestinian-teenager-dies-
notorious-israeli-megiddo-prison) in Megiddo.

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-
image-403778-2.png)

_On left: Majd Asadi_[ _in Megiddo
prison_](https://x.com/ireallyhateyou/status/2029384727057367452?s=20)
_earlier this month. On right: Asadi shortly after his release._

Following pressure from activists and lawyers, Asadi was
[released](https://www.sadanews.ps/en/news/282000.html) within days. The
conditions for his release included not posting anything about Iran or the war
for five days. He was also fined 4,000 shekels ($1290 dollars).

Asadi’s treatment is another example of the apartheid system Israel has
created for Palestinian citizens. Beyond the well-known
[dispossession](https://imeu.org/resources/resources/fact-sheet-palestinian-
citizens-of-israel/229) and
[exploitation](https://www.adalah.org/en/content/view/7771), this apartheid
manifests in tight surveillance of ’48 Palestinians’ speech, facilitated by
companies such as Facebook which [collaborate with
Israel](https://theintercept.com/2016/09/12/facebook-is-collaborating-with-
the-israeli-government-to-determine-what-should-be-censored/). In 2015, for
example, Palestinian poet Dareen Tatour was
[imprisoned](https://mondoweiss.net/2017/08/israel-nature-poetry/) and later
put on house arrest for posting a poem on Facebook titled [“Resist, My People,
Resist Them.”](https://arablit.org/2016/04/27/the-poem-for-which-dareen-
tatours-under-house-arrest-resist-my-people-resist-them/) For Palestinians who
aren’t citizens, the situation is obviously far worse than this baseline
apartheid. But stories like Asadi’s and Tatour’s debunk the idea that passport
holders live in any kind of “democracy.”

’48 Palestinians have long noted how Israel’s prisons shatter the myth of
Zionist democracy. In [_The
Pessoptimist_](https://archive.org/details/secretlifeofsaee0000abbi), a 1974
novel by Palestinian communist [Emile
Habibi](https://shortstoryproject.com/writers/emile-habiby/), a protagonist
named Saeed is repeatedly imprisoned for ridiculous violations. As Saeed is
taken to prison one time, his captors lecture him about the virtues of Israeli
democracy. “Our democracy is just not right for you people,” one Zionist says.
Once in the cell, Saeed is viciously beaten by a group of guards. Reality is
harsher than fiction: Palestinians face not only torture but also [lethal
rape](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/11/24/dying-in-hell-palestinian-
medics-jailed-by-israel), [extraction of
organs](https://thebaffler.com/latest/im-not-done-with-you-turfah), and other
horrors in Israeli prisons. As of September 2025, Israel held over 10,000
Palestinians under “administrative detection” (imprisonment without formal
charges or trial) or similar forms of incarceration justified by colonial
“security” reasons.

Yet this genocidal regime is [more
fragile](https://www.middleeasteye.net/opinion/Israel-unrestrained-brutality-
signals-beginning-of-its-end-how) than it may appear, which is why Israel
desperately tries to silence critical speech. Majd Asadi, however, is
undeterred. He left prison with renewed strength. “During my arrest, I didn’t
back down from anything,” Asadi
[wrote](https://www.facebook.com/majd.asadi/posts/%D7%99%D7%A9-%D7%A2%D7%9B%D7%A9%D7%99%D7%95-%D7%94%D7%A8%D7%91%D7%94-%D7%9E%D7%90%D7%95%D7%93-%D7%93%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%9C%D7%94%D7%AA%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%93%D7%93-%D7%90%D7%99%D7%AA%D7%9D-%D7%94%D7%A8%D7%91%D7%94-%D7%A7%D7%95%D7%A9%D7%99-%D7%95%D7%91%D7%A2%D7%99%D7%A7%D7%A8-%D7%A0%D7%99%D7%A6%D7%95%D7%9C-%D7%95%D7%A9%D7%99%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%99%D7%A0%D7%92%D7%90%D7%A0%D7%99-%D7%A2%D7%95%D7%91%D7%A8-%D7%95%D7%A1/10242482212294219/)
